disposition: existing direct food exposure, different outcomes
assessment: Healthy men consumed smoked and unsmoked powder in crossover. Primary methods and tables measure cardiovascular, metabolic, immune, and chemical markers. No Parkinson case or motor/speech endpoint.

disposition: companion direct food exposure, different outcomes
assessment: Smoked versus unsmoked feeding in the same protocol provided new glutathione and enzyme data. No neurologic task. Cohort identity is strongly indicated by named same recruitment and protocol.
Chemical assays distinguish grades even within a smoked production region. These are spice measurements with no clinical outcomes.

disposition: related animal outcome, same apparent study family
assessment: Isolated capsaicin MPTP abstracts report gait assessment. The poster describes abnormal steps and akinesia with no significant aggregate gait change. Neither accessible abstract provides an absolute stride contrast or freezing episode count.
A separate MPTP capsaicin study used rotarod balance and motor coordination. The assay does not record stride length or freezing episodes.
Jeong and colleagues reported chemically induced rotation in 6-OHDA mice after isolated capsaicin and glial measures. Asymmetric rotation is not the frozen gait outcome.

disposition: molecular follow-on, no new motor outcome
assessment: The article reuses 6-OHDA rat substantia-nigra material then tests transcript and cell apoptosis mechanisms. It reports no new cooking exposure or behavioral gait comparison.
Unspecified tremor in some acute severe presentations after isolated oral capsaicin. Parkinson rest tremor and culinary paprika were not tested.
Separate topical exposures and measured thumb tracking or precision pinch in adults without Parkinson disease. No handwriting task.
Typing and other sensorimotor learning tasks under capsaicin-induced skin pain. Task performance cannot establish changes in written letter size.
Tongue surface capsaicin during protrusion or force-targeting training. Studies record force accuracy and neurophysiology without a speech sample.
Post-stroke case used nebulized isolated compound and recorded pre/post vocal wetness in dysphagia care. No Parkinson intelligibility result.
Registry records and published rehabilitation use inhaled capsaicin as a cough challenge or cue, with no frozen intelligibility outcome.
Paprika exposure can be identified in parts of the clinical reports, with skin test or symptom context. No smoked preference or controlled spoken-intelligibility outcome.
The actual oral exposure was banana pepper, with paprika mentioned in prior literature. Case primarily assessed acute food allergy.
Localized capsaicin with heat in healthy volunteers. Controlled trials measured deliberately induced step-length asymmetry, its acquisition or retention, and no habitual Parkinson stride comparison.
